priority_tests.question: Do primary accounts of omissions, negative facts, and event ontology already distinguish when an absence obtains from when it becomes inevitable?
priority_tests.procedure: Search and read the closest primary texts identified by a fresh source phase; record exact queries, retrievals, and bounded passages. Compare their distinctions and truth conditions with closure time and criterion time.
priority_tests.decision_rule: If the same distinction and payoff are already explicit, mark novelty unestablished and either identify a narrower consequence or set aside the originality claim.

priority_tests.question: How do primary treatments of tense and future outcomes distinguish a presently settled future result from a completed deadline-relative claim?
priority_tests.procedure: Read primary treatments selected in a fresh source phase. Check whether the argument assumes present truth of future-tense propositions; revise if so.
priority_tests.decision_rule: Keep only the modal claim about open continuations unless a defensible account of future truth is supplied.

priority_tests.question: Does pre-deadline cancellation remove only the duty, or does it also end the identity of the task whose outcome is being assessed?
priority_tests.procedure: Compare an outcome benchmark that remains historically fixed, a norm that is waived, and an institutionally constituted task that terminates on cancellation. Ask what each statement evaluates.
priority_tests.decision_rule: If the task token has no stable criterion after cancellation, restrict the thesis to fixed outcome criteria and avoid calling the canceled task a failure.

priority_tests.question: Was the success route really closed?
priority_tests.procedure: Vary the case so that a substitute, reconstruction, waiver, or new route becomes available before the deadline. Separate objective possibility from the agent's knowledge or belief.
priority_tests.decision_rule: Use 'settled' only relative to explicitly stated live continuations; re-open the claim when a relevant route returns.

priority_tests.question: Does the distinction survive late performance and pure physical absence?
priority_tests.procedure: Compare on-time delivery, late delivery, a never-arriving package, and a physical absence with no task or deadline. Track the truth conditions of each description at closure, deadline, and afterward.
priority_tests.decision_rule: Keep the proposal limited to deadline-relative nonachievement if non-deadline absences have a different profile.

priority_tests.question: Does the deadline endpoint actually matter beyond reporting convention?
priority_tests.procedure: Construct a case where intervention becomes futile at c but the criterion time d affects a later evaluation, cancellation, or late-arrival judgment. Ask whether the proposed distinction changes any warranted explanation or responsibility judgment.
priority_tests.decision_rule: If no explanatory or practical difference survives after stipulations are made explicit, lower significance or set the proposal aside.
